posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Google co-founder Larry Page on why he'd give his fortune to Elon instead of to charity:

"THAT'S A WORTHY GOAL."

Charlie Rose: "Just simply giving it to Elon Musk, because you had confidence that he would change the future."

Larry Page: "He wants to go to Mars to back up humanity, that's a worthy goal, but it's a company."

That was on the TED stage in 2014, when SpaceX hadn't landed a single booster yet.

One of the richest men on Earth looked at a rocket company and saw the best place to put his money.

Charity spends money once. A company building toward Mars keeps paying it forward.

Mars is humanity's backup drive.

Video: TED / TED2014, "Where's Google going next?" Larry Page with Charlie Rose

quote.author: Napoleon__Bon
quote.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
quote.text:
Elon Musk on his grandfather in World War 2:

"My grandfather was in World War II for almost six years. All his friends got killed.

He's the only one of his friends to survive. And he was severely traumatized.

He really just couldn't even talk afterwards.

Most of that time was in East Africa, North Africa, Italy.

The only reason he's even alive frankly is because towards the end of the war they gave an aptitude test because he was just a corporal.

He didn't graduate high school so he wasn't eligible for officer school. And they plucked him out probably right before he died and sent him to work for British intelligence in London which is where he met my grandmother.

So he was one of the people fighting to stop the Nazis along with millions of others.

So let's not forget that the vast majority of the West fought and died to stop Nazism."

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
He who shapes power, data centers, chips and models into an economically feasible endpoint, disproportionately shapes AI/SI right now. 

Why?

Power is THE binding constraint in AI/SI. Few really have it. 

Data centers don’t work without power. This is not about promises of power tomorrow. Or forecasted power in 2028. Power TODAY. 

Chips can’t operate profitably unless installed in a functional data center. If you can install chips, it’s because you’ve solved the power problem. 

Models aren’t economically viable unless run on cost effective infrastructure which requires a functional data center with low input costs and reliable management. This can’t happen without power. 

AI/SI ROI doesn’t pencil unless models generate profitable outputs which necessarily needs functional data centers as the critical input. Again, power. 

Ergo, he who can shape data centers, chips and models together into a tightly coordinated stack is someone who has solved power. 

Solving power allows you to disproportionately shape AI/SI right now.
